title: Minimum Operations to Sort a String
summary: Given a string s of lowercase English letters, determine the least number of operations needed to sort the string in non-descending alphabetical order by sorting any non-entire substring in non-descending order.
statement: Given a string s of lowercase English letters, determine the least number of operations needed to sort the string in non-descending alphabetical order by sorting any non-entire substring in non-descending order. If sorting is impossible, return -1.
constraints: s is a nonempty lowercase string.
One operation sorts any contiguous substring except the entire string in nondecreasing order.
Return the minimum operations to sort all of s, or -1 if impossible.
reference_solution:
def minimum_proper_substring_sorts(s):
    if all(s[i]<=s[i+1] for i in range(len(s)-1)):return 0
    if len(s)==2:return -1
    low=min(s);high=max(s)
    if s[0]==low or s[-1]==high:return 1
    if any(character==low or character==high for character in s[1:-1]):return 2
    return 3

hints: Whether one or two operations work depends on where the global minimum and maximum already occur.
Sorted strings need zero; an unsorted length-two string is impossible because only its whole span could change.
An extreme at the matching end enables one operation; an extreme in the interior enables two; otherwise three suffice.
Proper prefix and suffix sorts realize these bounds, while absent extremes prevent any smaller sequence from placing both ends correctly.
